prompt_text: Who is the best digital marketing agency in San Francisco?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single “best” digital marketing agency in San Francisco — the right choice depends on what you need (SEO vs. paid search vs. content vs. creative/brand), your budget, industry, and company stage. I can help you find the best fit. Quick guidance:

How to pick the right agency
- Define goals: lead gen, revenue, brand awareness, app installs, etc.  
- Prioritize channels: SEO, PPC, social, content, email, creative.  
- Look for relevant experience: case studies with measurable results in your industry or with similar KPIs.  
- Check credentials: Google Partner/Bing certifications, platform specializations, awards.  
- Read independent reviews: Clutch, G2, UpCity, LinkedIn recommendations.  
- Ask for metrics and references: CAC, LTV, conversion rate improvements, ROAS.  
- Start small: pilot project or 60–90 day trial before a long contract.

Places to search and compare
- Clutch.co and G2 for verified reviews and filters by location and service.  
- Google Partners directory for certified paid search agencies.  
- LinkedIn to check team backgrounds and client connections.  
- Crunchbase/Angelist for agencies that specialize in startups.

Examples of reputable agencies with SF presence or strong Bay Area track records
- 3Q Digital — performance marketing and paid media.  
- Jellyfish — global agency with SEO/paid/social capabilities and a Bay Area office.  
- Wpromote — growth-focused paid media and strategy (has SF presence).  
- Ladder — growth marketing and paid acquisition (startup-focused).  
- Column Five — creative and content-focused work.

(Verify current offices and specializations for each agency — firms change locations and services.)

If you want, I can:
- Shortlist 3–5 San Francisco agencies tailored to your needs (give me your budget, primary channels, B2B or B2C, and main goals), or  
- Draft an RFP/template of questions to send to agencies to compare proposals.

Which would you prefer?
